name: Gaple
description: Gaple is a popular Indonesian block domino game played on a single train line. Players add matching tiles at either end, and if blocked they either discard a dead tile or pass depending on table rules.

overview.description: Gaple is a popular Indonesian block domino game played on a single train line. Players add matching tiles at either end, and if blocked they either discard a dead tile or pass depending on table rules.

history.origins: Gaple developed as an Indonesian local form of block dominoes using western double-six tiles.
timeline: 20th century: Gaple spread widely through social play in Indonesian communities.
Modern era: It remains one of the most common casual domino games in Indonesia.
history.cultural: Gaple is a staple social game and is often played in informal money or chip settlements.
history.evolution: Local rules preserved the single-train structure but developed distinct blocked-hand and dead-tile handling.

setup.players: Four or five players. With four, play can be individual or partnerships; with five, individual play.
setup.dealing: Four-player variants use either 6 each (4 face-down in center) or 7 each (no center tiles). Five-player game deals 5 each (3 face-down in center).

rules.objective: Be left with the lowest pip total when the hand ends, either by going out or by blocked play.
rules.gameplay: Play proceeds on a single train, adding one matching tile to either open end. In hands with undealt center tiles, one center tile is exposed to start the line. In 4-player 7-tile play, the double blank 0-0 starts the first hand and later hands begin with a double from the previous winner side. A blocked player usually discards one dead tile face down; some tables use pass-only handling.
keyRules: Unplayed tiles, including dead tiles, count as penalty pips at hand end.
Common tie-breaker: lowest single tile wins ties on total pips; if still tied, lowest end wins.
Some tables count the double blank 0-0 as 25 only when no other blank tile remains in that hand.

strategy.basic: Unload high-pip doubles early; stranded heavy tiles are costly in blocked endings.
strategy.intermediate: Track which pip numbers are saturated to predict blocked ends and preserve flexible connectors.
strategy.advanced: In dead-tile play, choose dead discards that minimize your own penalty while reducing opponents' line options.
tips: Remember there are seven copies of each pip number in a double-six set.
When low on options, protect low-value singles for tie-break situations.
Adjust aggression based on whether blocked players discard dead tiles or simply pass.

variations.name: Four Player Six-Tile Deal
variations.description: Each player takes six tiles, leaving four face down; one center tile is exposed to start.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal size and center-tile setup differ from base; engine overrides not yet mapped.

variations.name: Pass-Only Blocking
variations.description: When blocked, players pass and keep all tiles in hand instead of discarding dead tiles.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Blocked-hand branch (pass vs discard) is procedural; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Double-Blank 25 Rule
variations.description: At scoring, the double blank 0-0 counts 25 only if the player holds no other blank tile.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional scoring rule for 0-0; scoring override not yet mapped to engine.

scoring.description: At hand end, each player totals pips on all unplayed tiles, including dead tiles if used. Lowest total wins the hand.
scoring.winCondition: Winner is the player with least points; ties are broken by lowest single tile, then lowest end value.

synthesis.shortDescription: Indonesian single-train domino game for four or five players with blocked-hand and dead-tile variants.
